//: Copy this file to agent-queue.config.json (gitignored) and fill it in. Keys ending in Note, and every "//" key, are documentation and are ignored on load. docs/configuration.md explains every key.

human.name: Alex
human.nameNote: The person the queue works for. It appears in prompts, worker briefs, ticket comments and Slack lines ("ask Alex", "waiting on Alex's answer").

orchestrator.sessionNameNote: The pinned Claude Code session that writes specs and watches the queue. Emergency responders message it by this name.

repoPathNote: The local main checkout of the repo the queue builds. Workers cut their worktrees from it; the pre-merge check keeps its scratch worktree under it.
workspaceCwdNote: The folder workers start in (fleet.sh dispatch --cwd). Usually the repo's parent, so a worker can see sibling repos.
worktreesDirNote: Where worktrees live, relative to repoPath.

paths.stateDirNote: Per machine: state.json, logs, the PAUSED flag, the tick lock, and the secret files (slack-webhook, slack-bot-token, linear-api-key).
paths.sharedDirNote: Shared across machines. Point it at a folder Syncthing or Dropbox keeps in sync when more than one machine runs the queue. Holds merge-requests/, heartbeats/, bundles/ and main-state.json.

github.repoNote: owner/name of the repo the queue builds.
github.userNote: The gh account the dispatcher and the merge scripts act as (gh auth token --user).
github.baseBranchNote: The branch PRs target and the main watcher reads.
github.ciWorkflowNote: The workflow name the pre-merge check and the main watcher read.
github.reviewCheckNote: The status check that must pass before a PR counts as green. Set it to null to skip the review check.
github.rerunLabelNote: merge-when-ready.sh adds this label once when the review check reads "Re-review not requested". Set it to null if your review bot re-runs on every push.
github.fixesMainLabelNote: A PR with this label (or a revert) may merge while main is red.
github.branchTemplateNote: The branch a worker builds on. {id} is the lowercased ticket ID, so ENG-123 builds on agent/eng-123.

linear.teamNote: The team key. It is also the ticket prefix (ENG-123).
linear.apiKeyCommandNote: Optional argv that prints the Linear API key, for a secrets manager, e.g. ["doppler", "secrets", "get", "LINEAR_API_KEY", "--plain"]. The LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable wins over it; with neither, the key is read from apiKeyFile.
linear.apiKeyFileNote: The file holding the Linear API key when neither the environment nor apiKeyCommand gives one. Mode 600.
linear.inboxProjectNote: The Linear project ask-human.sh files an ask into when the ask is not about a ticket.
linear.sizeLabelGroupNote: The Linear label group whose child labels (S, M, L) size a ticket.

labels.labelsNote: ready, building and stuck are the queue's state machine. needsHuman marks a ticket with an open ask. sentry, mechanical and judgment drive the Sentry lane; leave them as they are if you have no Sentry triage.

states.statesNote: Workflow state names on the team. A claimed ticket moves to inProgress; a merged one to verifying.

linear.verifyEvidenceHeadingNote: merged-to-verifying.mjs leaves a ticket in Done only when its newest comment with this heading came after the merge and has no FAIL cell.

slack.domainNote: The subdomain in https://<domain>.slack.com, used to build thread links.
slack.channelNote: The channel ID asks and progress lines go to. Keep the channel private: it carries ticket titles.
slack.channelNameNote: The channel's display name, used in docs and prompts.
slack.webhookFileNote: An incoming-webhook URL for progress lines (started, PR opened, merged). Mode 600. Missing means no progress posts.
slack.botTokenFileNote: A bot token with chat:write, for asks and the reviewer DM. Mode 600. Missing means asks stay in Linear until a machine that has it sweeps them.

reviewer.name: Sam
reviewer.nameNote: How prompts, notes and ticket comments name the reviewer.
reviewer.githubNote: Their GitHub login: requested as reviewer, and the only login whose review counts for a judgment PR.
reviewer.slackUserNote: Their Slack user ID, for the one DM per PR.
reviewer.fallbackChannelNote: Where the DM goes, with a mention, when Slack refuses it (the app's Messages tab is off).
reviewer.reviewerNote: The human who reviews judgment-path Sentry fixes. The dispatcher requests their GitHub review, comments the ticket, and DMs them once per PR; if the DM is refused it posts in fallbackChannel with a mention. Only judgment-path PRs wait on them.

fleet.primaryAccountNote: The account whose config dir is ~/.claude, which the human's own sessions use. The dispatcher spreads work away from it. fleet.sh always gives ~/.claude the label a, so keep this at "a".
fleet.mainCheckoutWritableDirsNote: Folders under repoPath that fleet/hooks/protect-main-checkout.sh leaves open to file writes (git run from inside them stays blocked), e.g. [".claude/builds"] for a build skill's state. Name only folders the repo's .gitignore ignores. The worktree folder (worktreesDir) is always open.

dispatcher.enabledHostsNote: Short hostnames (hostname -s) that run ticks. A host missing here does nothing.

hosts.hostsNote: Per machine: maxWorkers caps working fleet workers there (queue and outside ones). accounts limits which fleet accounts it may use; fallbackAccounts get work only when no regular account can take it. maxLoadPerCore and minMemoryFreePercent override the defaults below. sentryWorkers are side slots kept for Sentry tickets.

dispatcher.maxConcurrentNote: Workers across all machines, counted through the building label. A bundle counts as one.
dispatcher.maxDispatchesPerDayNote: null means no daily cap; worker slots and maxConcurrent still bound the queue.
dispatcher.maxLoadPerCoreNote: A machine whose 5-minute load average is over this times its core count claims nothing that tick.
dispatcher.minMemoryFreePercentNote: A machine with less memory free than this claims nothing that tick (macOS memory pressure level, or MemAvailable on Linux).
dispatcher.headroomFloorPercentNote: An account needs at least this much left in both its 5-hour and weekly windows to get work.
dispatcher.workerCapNote: fleet.sh --max-workers for each dispatch: working background sessions one account may hold.
dispatcher.stallHoursNote: Hours with nothing moving (no commit, no PR activity, worker not busy) before the human gets one stall note. A ticket goes stuck only when its worker has also ended.
dispatcher.spinHoursNote: Hours a worker may stay busy without a commit or PR change before it counts as stalled.
dispatcher.longRunNoticeHoursNote: An informational "still going" Slack line every this many hours of a ticket's build.
dispatcher.stuckInARowTripsNote: This many stuck tickets in a row pause the dispatcher.
dispatcher.maxRedispatchesNote: Replacement workers a ticket gets when its worker's session dies (a reboot, say) before it can go stuck.
dispatcher.flakeWaitMinutesNote: How long a failure on a merge commit waits for a later main commit to pass the same workflow before it pauses the queue.
dispatcher.modelNote: The model every queue worker runs (fleet.sh dispatch --model).
dispatcher.effortNote: The reasoning effort every queue worker runs at (low, medium, high, xhigh, max).
dispatcher.permissionModeNote: The Claude Code permission mode for queue workers and the red-main responder (fleet.sh dispatch --mode). null keeps fleet.sh's default, bypassPermissions: workers run unattended, and one that stops at a permission prompt has stalled. In that mode a worker can run any command your user can, so run the queue under a user and on a machine where that is acceptable. A stricter mode (auto, acceptEdits) trades that for workers that may stop and wait.
dispatcher.notifyNote: macOS notifications per transition. Linux hosts rely on Slack.
dispatcher.queueSizesNote: Size labels the queue takes. A ready ticket with another size is sent back.
dispatcher.riskyPathPatternsNote: Matched case-insensitively against every changed path and rename source. A green PR touching one goes to the orchestrator session for review and merge (shared merge-requests/).
dispatcher.bundleNote: Up to maxTickets linked agent-ready tickets from one project, of a size in sizes, ride on one worker and one PR. A ticket whose description has a 'Ships alone: <reason>' line never bundles.
dispatcher.sentryHeartbeatMinutesNote: While a host with sentryWorkers wrote its heartbeat (sharedDir/heartbeats) under this many minutes ago and is unpaused, other machines leave Sentry tickets to it.
dispatcher.sentryTriageNote: An optional triage module you write (this repo ships none), loaded from dispatcher/ on host only, behind enabled. It exports kickFromTick({ cfg, dry, log }), which should start its run in a detached process, and statusLine(cfg). It labels the tickets it queues with linear.labels.sentry plus mechanical or judgment. A throw or syntax error in it is one log line and never stops a tick.

push.gatesNote: Commands gated-push.mjs runs in the worktree before pushing, each an argv array. A failing gate fails the push.
push.envNote: Extra environment for the git push itself, e.g. {"SKIP_PREPUSH": "1"} when gates above replace a slow pre-push hook.

premerge.installCommandNote: Runs in the scratch worktree before the check. null or [] skips it.
premerge.checkCommandNote: Runs in the scratch worktree after current main is merged into the PR. {base} is replaced with the main commit the PR's CI ran against, for a check that only covers what changed since.
premerge.errorPatternNote: A failing check counts as a real failure only when its output matches this. Anything else (killed, timed out) holds the merge a tick instead.
premerge.copyFilesNote: Files copied from repoPath into the scratch worktree when it is first made (gitignored files the check needs).
premerge.buildOutputRootsNote: Each package under these folders has its dist/ and *.tsbuildinfo cleared before the check, so a previous check's output never shadows this tree.
premerge.migrationsNote: Two PRs that each pick the same migration prefix pass alone and clash once merged. Set to null if your migrations have no ordered prefix.
premerge.actionlintNote: When the merged workflows differ from main's, lint both with actionlint (if installed) and fail on findings main does not have. false skips it.

mainWatch.accountsNote: Fleet accounts an emergency responder may run on.
mainWatch.modelNote: The model the emergency responder runs.
mainWatch.maxWorkersNote: fleet.sh --max-workers for the responder, set high so it starts beyond the regular worker cap.
mainWatch.realertMinutesNote: While main stays red, alert again every this many minutes.
mainWatch.maxRespondersNote: Responders started per red streak (a second one only when the first has ended).
mainWatch.ignoreJobsNote: CI job names to leave out of the failing-jobs list (an aggregate job that only reports the others, say).

queueBoard.hostNote: The short hostname (hostname -s) of the machine that runs the board. One board covers every queue machine. hourly-check.mjs reads the board on loopback there, and by this name from any other machine. Leave it null to mean the machine the script runs on.
queueBoard.portNote: The board's port. The QUEUE_BOARD_PORT environment variable wins over it.
queueBoard.bindNote: Addresses the board listens on. Literal addresses are bound at start; the word "tailscale" binds this machine's Tailscale address (tailscale ip -4) once Tailscale is up, so your other devices on the tailnet can open the board. Keep it off the LAN and 0.0.0.0: anyone who can reach the board can type into a worker's session.
queueBoard.sshNote: How the board reaches each other host in dispatcher.enabledHosts: an ssh destination (an alias from ~/.ssh/config works). A host missing here is reached by its own name. The board's own host is read directly; its entry, if any, only builds the copyable ssh attach command for a viewer on another machine. Needs key-based login (BatchMode).
queueBoard.namesNote: Short names the page shows for each host. A host missing here shows its hostname.
queueBoard.remoteRootNote: Where this repo is checked out on the other hosts. The board runs node <remoteRoot>/queue-board/collect.mjs (and history.mjs, worktrees.mjs, ext-usage.mjs, send.py) there over ssh, and those read that host's own agent-queue.config.json, so each host finds its own paths.stateDir. A path that starts with ~/, or sits under the board machine's home, is taken relative to each host's own home. null means the same place as this checkout on the board's host.
queueBoard.repoRootsNote: Folders whose direct child git repos the Worktrees view scans on every host. Include the folder that holds repoPath. Defaults to workspaceCwd.
queueBoard.extUsageNote: Show the Codex and Grok plan usage of every host (ext-usage.mjs asks each CLI's read-only billing call once an hour). false turns it off when you have neither CLI.
queueBoard.healthUrlNote: A URL on the environment your base branch deploys to (staging), answering JSON with a commit field. hourly-check.mjs reports when it serves an older commit than the branch head for over 2 hours. null skips that check, e.g. "https://api.staging.example.com/health".

learning.outDirNote: Where the sweep keeps reports/, history.json and cache/. null means <paths.stateDir>/learning. Keep it outside the repo: it holds run data.
learning.ciWorkflowFileNote: The workflow file the CI source reads, e.g. "ci.yml". null finds the workflow named github.ciWorkflow through the Actions API.
learning.skipJobsNote: Regexes (case-insensitive) for CI job names the CI source leaves out: aggregate or watcher jobs that fail only because another job did, and the review check's job, whose findings the review source counts on their own.
learning.reviewBotLoginNote: The GitHub login whose inline PR review comments count as review findings. A finding's first line reads **[Axis]** Severity: RULE-ID text.
learning.reviewRulesGlobNote: Optional glob under repoPath, e.g. "docs/standards/*.md", for markdown tables of review rules (| TST-21 | Rule name |). The report names a rule with them. null shows rule IDs only.
learning.correctionsGlobNote: Optional glob for the human's feedback memory files, e.g. "~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/feedback_*.md". Each new or changed file counts as a correction. null turns the source off.
learning.sshNote: Other machines whose dispatcher.log the sweep reads, as {"<short hostname>": "user@host"}, e.g. {"linux-box": "you@linux-box"}. The log is read from the same stateDir under the remote home. The local machine is always read from disk; --no-ssh skips these.

catalog.title: PR body has no machine-read "Fix:" line in ## Regression proof
catalog.why: CI already rejects it, which is where the cost comes from. Shift it left: a pre-push or PR-create check that reads the body before CI runs, or a generated body that always carries the line.

learning.catalogNote: Failure types of your own, checked before the built-in ones (typecheck, lint, network flake, Postgres connection terminated, out of memory). match is a regex source run against "<job> <signature>" (flags default to i); enforce lists strings whose presence in an enforcement source counts as enforced there; recommend is a fix-ladder level 1 to 6. The example is a PR-template line CI requires; replace it with the line your PR check requires, or set [] if you have none.
learning.enforcementSourcesNote: Extra files or folders searched for a type's enforce strings, each with its fix-ladder level. pattern filters a folder's files (default: every file not starting with a dot). Always searched: repoPath's ESLint config (2), .github/workflows and .husky (3), the PR template (4), its CLAUDE.md (5), ~/.claude/settings.json (3), dispatcher/worker-brief.md and specdesk/SPECDESK.md (4), ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (5).
learning.draftStateNote: The workflow state learning/linear.mjs create files a drafted fix ticket in. It never adds the ready label.
